questions.statement: Which command asks a student to close the window?

options.feedback: 'Shut down' applies to machines, not to windows.
'Close' is the verb used with a window or a door.
'Open' is the opposite action.
'Break' would be a destructive instruction.

questions.explanation:
El verbo 'close' se usa para ventanas y puertas; 'turn off' es para aparatos. Esta estructura se repite con otros sustantivos del mismo grupo.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Look at this instruction: 'Don't run in the hallway.' What does it mean?

options.text: You can run in the hallway.
options.feedback: 'Don't' negates the action instead of allowing it.

options.text: You should run in the hallway.
options.feedback: 'Don't' states a prohibition, not a suggestion.

options.text: You must run in the hallway.
options.feedback: That is the opposite of the instruction given.

options.text: You must not run in the hallway.
options.feedback: 'Don't' plus the base verb expresses a prohibition.

questions.explanation:
'Don't' es la forma negativa del imperativo: prohibe la accion de correr en el pasillo.

questions.statement: Which sentence is a polite request?

options.feedback: 'Could you... please?' is a polite request in question form.
The bare imperative is a command, not a polite request.
'Must' imposes an obligation.
That is a statement about behaviour, not a request.

questions.explanation:
Las peticiones amables suelen usar 'Could' o 'Can' con 'please'; la forma imperativa es mas directa.

questions.statement: Choose the correct response to the instruction: 'Put your books on the desk.'

options.text: My books are on the table.
options.feedback: A statement about location does not respond to the command.

options.text: I put my books on the desk.
options.feedback: The student carries out the instruction given.

options.text: I want to put my books there.
options.feedback: 'Want to' expresses a wish, not compliance.

options.text: The books put on the desk.
options.feedback: That order of words is not a grammatical English sentence.

questions.explanation:
La respuesta correcta ejecuta la orden: coloca los libros sobre el escritorio. La regla se aprende junto con los demas ejemplos de la unidad.

questions.statement: What does the teacher mean by 'Please take your seats'?

options.feedback: Nothing in the sentence mentions leaving.
'Take your seats' has nothing to do with the window.

options.text: Sit down in your assigned seats.
options.feedback: 'Take your seats' means to go and sit in your place.

options.text: Give your books to the teacher.
options.feedback: That would be 'hand in your books', a different instruction.

questions.explanation:
La instruccion pide a los estudiantes que ocupen sus asientos, no que se levanten. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.statement: Choose the word that completes: 'Don't talk while the teacher is ____.'

options.feedback: 'While' requires the present continuous for an action in progress.
'Spoke' is the simple past and does not fit 'while'.
'Speaking' fits 'while' plus the present continuous sense.
'Spoken' is a past participle and cannot follow 'while' here.

questions.explanation:
'Speaking' describe la accion de hablar en ese momento. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.statement: Which sentence gives an instruction politely?

options.feedback: The bare imperative sounds direct and unfriendly.
'Will' imposes an instruction, not a request.
That is a statement of obligation, not a request.

options.text: Would you mind opening the window?
options.feedback: 'Would you mind' plus -ing is a standard polite request.

questions.explanation:
'Would you mind opening the window?' es una formula cortese; el imperativo directo seria mas brusco.

questions.statement: What is the opposite of the instruction 'Stand up'?

options.feedback: 'Sit down' is the direct opposite of 'stand up'.
'Look up' refers to the direction of the eyes, not posture.
'Stand still' still requires standing, only motionless.
'Lie down' is a different action, not the direct opposite.

questions.explanation:
'Sit down' es la instruccion contraria a 'stand up'. Conviene practicarlo con otros ejemplos antes del examen.
